request.spec:
The header shows the signed-in user's crew total when a person with the user's name leads a
crew: the due-totals of the crews they lead, added up; nothing otherwise.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
The header shows the signed-in user's crew total when a person with the user's name leads a
crew: the due-totals of the crews they lead, added up; nothing otherwise.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as

AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The header now shows the signed-in user's crew total, and all 4 tests in `bin/e2e` pass.

**How it works:** The header has a new "My crews' due" value (`my-crew-due-total`). It finds the person whose name or alias matches the signed-in user (ignoring case) — the same person "My due" uses. It then adds up the due-totals of every crew that person leads. If no such person exists, or they lead no crew, it's blank. If they lead crews that have no due figures at all, it shows `0.00`.

**What changed (front end only):** Crews and their due-totals were already loaded and worked out in the browser, so nothing on the server, in the database or in the audit file needed to change.
- `features/crews/crews.ts`: I moved the crew due-total sum into a shared `crewDueCents()` function, so the crew rows and the header total use the same calculation.
- `features/people/people.ts`: the person matching the signed-in user is now looked up in one place (`me`), which both "My due" and the new `myCrewDue` total use.
- `features/counters/counters.ts`: displays the new value in the header.
